cases.heading: Named fields
cases.prose: A row marked =_= names the field below each of its cells; a row marked =^= names the field above. A name can then stand for that field on the right of a formula, or be the target on the left: =$tax== writes that one field.
cases.input:
|   | Price | Tax | Total |
| _ | price | tax | total |
| # |   100 |     |       |
#+TBLFM: $tax=$price*0.2;%.2f::$total=$price*1.2;%.2f
cases.emacs:
|   | Price | Tax   | Total  |
| _ | price | tax   | total  |
| # | 100   | 20.00 | 120.00 |
#+TBLFM: $tax=$price*0.2;%.2f::$total=$price*1.2;%.2f

cases.heading: A default format
cases.prose: A =$= row can hold =%== and a format. It is added to a formula that has flags such as =N= but no format of its own, so one line sets the decimals for the table. A formula with no flags at all does not get it.

cases.heading: Several formulas, in order
cases.prose: Formulas do not run in the order written. Org sorts them by their target, and runs column formulas row by row before field formulas, so a formula sees the results of the ones that sort before it. Here =$3= is written first but runs after =$2=.
